issues.title: Background and foreground colors do not have a sufficient contrast ratio.
issues.action: Low-contrast text is difficult or impossible for many users to read. Learn how to provide sufficient color contrast.

issues.title: Heading elements are not in a sequentially-descending order

issues.title: Image elements do not have [alt] attributes
issues.action: Informative elements should aim for short, descriptive alternate text. Decorative elements can be ignored with an empty alt attribute. Learn more about the alt attribute.

issues.title: Links do not have a discernible name
issues.action: Link text (and alternate text for images, when used as links) that is discernible, unique, and focusable improves the navigation experience for screen reader users. Learn how to make links accessible.

issues.title: Select elements do not have associated label elements.

issues.title: Touch targets do not have sufficient size or spacing.
issues.action: Touch targets with sufficient size and spacing help users who may have difficulty targeting small controls to activate the targets. Learn more about touch targets.

issues.title: Elements with role="none" or role="presentation" have conflicts
issues.action: There are certain cases where the semantic role of an element with role="none" or role="presentation" does not resolve to none or presentation. To ensure the element remains removed from the accessibility tree, you should not add any global ARIA attributes to the element or make it focusable. Learn more about presentation role conflict.
